title: In-situ Multi-modal STEM Investigation of Electromigration-induced Failure in Cu Thin Films
content: Electromigration (EM) remains a critical reliability challenge in microelectronic devices, where the migration of atoms under high current densities leads to structural degradation, void formation, and eventual failure of copper (Cu) interconnects [1,2]. As device dimensions shrink, understanding the microstructural evolution under EM stress is essential for improving interconnect reliability [3]. However, direct observation of EM-induced changes at the nanoscale is challenging due to the dynamic nature of defect formation and the requirement for high-resolution imaging techniques.
